creative.body:
I was standing in my kitchen at 11pm last March, holding a glass of Metamucil that was already turning into pudding before I could finish drinking it, when I finally said it out loud to myself.

"I take fiber supplements but I don't know if it's really working."

That sentence had been sitting in the back of my head for 6 months. Every morning with the Metamucil. Every night with the psyllium husk. Every Tuesday at CVS putting another box of fiber into my cart because the last 1 hadn't done anything.

I'd been choking that powder down twice a day for half a year. My doctor told me it would fix the constipation Wegovy was giving me. It didn't. It made it worse.

I poured the pudding glass down the drain.

I am 57. Down 36 pounds on Wegovy by that night. My jeans fit. My knees stopped hurting. People at church asking what I was doing.

Everything was working except 1 thing. I had stopped going to the bathroom.

By month 4 my kitchen cabinet looked like a fiber convention.

Metamucil at 7am. Benefiber in my coffee at 9am. Fiber gummies at 11am. Psyllium at lunch. Chia in my afternoon yogurt. Citrucel before dinner. Acacia powder before bed.

6 different products. Around 50 grams of fiber a day. Easily double what I had ever eaten before Wegovy.

My bowel kept getting worse. 7 days no movement. 9 days. Once, 11.

Every appointment with my GI was the same conversation, with the fiber recommendation getting bigger.

Month 1 she said add psyllium husk in the morning. Month 2 she said double the psyllium and add Benefiber at lunch. Month 3 she said try Citrucel, some patients respond to that one. Month 4 she said add the acacia powder and the fiber gummies in the afternoon.

Every appointment, another product into the cart. Never a question about whether the last one had worked.

The morning after the 11-day mark she did not look at me. She looked at her chart. "Try Citrucel instead. Some patients respond to that. And add Miralax twice a day."

I drove home with another box in the passenger seat.

That was the night of the Metamucil pudding.

My husband had gone to bed. I sat at my kitchen table with my phone and I did not get up until almost 3 in the morning.

I did this for 8 nights in a row.

So I started reading. Here is what I found, night by night.

Night 1.

Reddit. The Wegovy sub. Constipation thread after constipation thread.

The first comment that stopped me was buried 40 replies deep on a thread that had been up for 7 hours.

"My main nutrition concern before Wegovy was fiber. I aimed for 50g a day. Learned real quick that wasn't going to fly. That insane amount just sat and built up in my slowed-down GI."

A woman in Ohio. 4 months ahead of me. Same medication. Same exact failure I was living, written by a stranger before I had the words for it. I sat with my phone in my hand and read that sentence 4 times.

Night 2.

I went back. The Mounjaro sub. The Ozempic sub. r/GLP1 hidden behind a karma wall I did not have. I read until my eyes burned.

The fiber comments were everywhere. The laxative comments were the ones that scared me.

"Be careful with stool softeners and laxatives daily. You don't want your body to get used to them. Speaking from experience here. I was on Miralax 14 months and my body forgot how to go without it. Now my GI is talking about magnesium dependency on top of it. I would give anything to go back."

I had been on daily Miralax for 6 weeks. I had already started doubling. I closed the laptop and sat in the dark for a while.

Night 3.

I had stopped reading Reddit and started reading the older constipation forums. The ones from 2014. 2016.

Different medications. Different surgeries. Different diagnoses. Same product list that had failed all of them.

Halfway through one of the 2016 threads I saw a word I had never seen attached to my own problem before. Gastric. As in stomach. Not colon. A woman in the thread had written that her surgeon had told her her constipation was actually delayed gastric emptying, and the laxatives she had been on for a year were not designed for the place her food was actually stuck.

I underlined the word in my notebook.

Night 4.

I went to PubMed at 1am.

I want to tell you I knew what I was doing. I did not. I was a 57 year old woman with a search bar and a glass of water at 1 in the morning. But I learned to skim the abstracts. I learned the search terms. Gastric emptying. Delayed gastric motility. GLP-1 receptor agonist. Apigenin smooth muscle.

That was the night the picture clicked.

The medication is doing 2 separate things to my body. Not 1. The first is happening in my brain. The appetite suppression. The part that makes me eat less. That is the engine of my weight loss, the 36 pounds, the jeans, the knees. I do not want to undo that part. The second is happening in my stomach. Not my colon. My stomach. The medication has taken my stomach from normal to nearly frozen. Food that should leave in 4 hours is sitting there for 10 or 12. While it sits there, bacteria ferment it. The gas, the bloating, the constipation, the 4pm pressure, all of it is coming from the stomach, not the colon.

I sat at the kitchen table at 1:30am and worked it out.

Night 5.

The reframe took the next night to land all the way.

I drew the system in my head. Stomach at the top. 6 feet of intestine in the middle. Colon at the bottom. The medication had stopped my stomach. Every fiber product I had been choking down was designed to add bulk to my colon. Every laxative was designed to pull water into my colon.

Every product on every shelf I had ever tried worked 6 feet downstream from where the actual problem was sitting.

I had been packing more cargo onto a truck that had not left the loading dock. No wonder I was getting bigger by dinner. No wonder Miralax barely did anything anymore. The Miralax was flushing an empty pipe.

Night 6.

I went looking for what does work on the stomach.

That was the night I found apigenin. A plant compound concentrated in celery juice. Described as a prokinetic. Working on the smooth muscle of the stomach wall. Helping the contractions start again. Not a laxative. Not a stimulant. Not a fiber. The brain part of the medication, the appetite suppression, the engine of the weight loss, was not affected.

The dose was the catch. The clinical research used 30 to 50mg of standardized apigenin extract. Most of the celery capsules I found on Amazon were 500mg of celery powder, which contains less than 0.1% apigenin by weight. The women in the reviews complaining apigenin did not work were taking less than 1 milligram a day. They thought apigenin did not work. It did. They had been taking nothing.

Night 7.

I went back to the GLP-1 forums with a new search.

I found the thread on the third forum I tried. 14 women, 80 replies. 3 of them in their 60s, in their own words and from their own accounts, had each named the same product. None of them seemed to know each other. They had each been on a GLP-1 over a year. Off Miralax for months. Bloating gone. Eating dinner again.

A small company called Motilli. Heart-shaped gummies. 2 a day. Standardized apigenin extract from celery, not powder. Combined with chlorophyllin, which one of them said had taken her bloating to nothing in a week, and a small targeted dose of soluble prebiotic that was a fraction of the bulk-fiber dose I had been choking down.

Night 8.

I read for 2 more hours, looking for a reason not to.

I could not find one. The gummy was the part that mattered for me. A gummy is pre-dissolved. It does not need to be broken down by a stomach that has already stopped breaking things down. The 90-day money-back guarantee was the only reason I hit the button after 6 fiber products and Miralax had burned me.

I ordered it at 1:47am on night 8.

I closed the laptop. I went to bed. I did not read another forum thread for 6 weeks.

The bottle arrived 3 days later. Days 1 through 4 nothing. Day 5 the 4pm pressure was not as sharp. Day 9 I went on my own with no Miralax, no Metamucil, no psyllium. Day 14 I ate a full plate of pasta and laughed at a movie 3 hours later without thinking about my stomach once. Week 4 I took the Metamucil, Benefiber, psyllium, Citrucel, acacia, fiber gummies, and Miralax off my counter and put them in a trash bag. Week 6 my husband saw the empty counter and said, "Took you long enough."

If you are the woman tonight standing in her kitchen with a glass of Metamucil turning into pudding, I am writing this for you.

You are not crazy. The fiber is making it worse. The Miralax is going to stop working. Your body is telling you something every doctor you have seen so far is not.

The medication works in 2 places. Brain part is the engine. Don't undo it. Stomach part is the side effect. Every product on every shelf works 6 feet downstream. Apigenin works on the right organ.

I am not affiliated with the company. Motilli runs a 90-day money-back guarantee. The bottles sell out for stretches because apigenin degrades from light and heat, so they batch-produce. If you have a vacation, a holiday, a wedding coming up, I would not wait until next week.

The link is below.

P.S. I think about night 7 a lot. The thread where 3 strangers had named the same product. I want you to find this before you have to do night 1 through night 8 alone the way I did. The link is below.
